name: Petrobras Tramandaí oil spill
place: Sea and beaches off Tramandaí, Rio Grande do Sul
affected: Beaches closed to public use.
damage: 18,000 litres of oil; Ibama found about ten metres of permanent preservation area polluted.
legal_outcome: Federal prosecutors' civil action. Federal Environmental Court of Porto Alegre ordered more than R$ 6 million (R$ 3,045,229.64 for environmental damage plus the same for collective moral damages) and emergency plans within 90 days. Reported 13 Aug 2013, 13 years later.
summary: Petrobras spilled 18,000 litres of oil off Tramandaí in January 2000. A court only ruled in 2013. A separate 2012 monobuoy spill exists but its size is not confirmed.

name: Osasco Plaza Shopping gas explosion
place: Food court, Osasco, São Paulo
operator: Private shopping company (B Sete Participações and Administradora do Osasco Plaza Shopping); gas supplied by Ultragaz
affected: 472 injured (Conjur); other reports give 300 to 372.
damage: Gas leak in the buried distribution network; shops reported a gas smell long before.
legal_outcome: June 1999: TJ-SP ordered owners and administrators to compensate victims, upheld by STJ. Feb 2005: TJ-SP criminal chamber acquitted the administrator, an engineer and three construction engineers. 2006: TJ-SP held the shopping administrator, not Ultragaz, responsible for inspection.
summary: A gas leak exploded in the food court, killing 42 people. The criminal case ended in acquittals nine years later. The shopping blames construction and gas-company inspection failures and sued Ultragaz; the court has sided with Ultragaz so far.

name: Vila Socó pipeline fire
place: Vila Socó, Cubatão, São Paulo
deaths: Disputed: 93 official; 508 (MPSP); up to about 700 in other estimates.
affected: About 6,000 residents lived in the stilt-house favela.
damage: About 700,000 litres of gasoline leaked under stilt houses and ignited.
legal_outcome: 24 people charged; 7 engineers and employees sentenced to 1 year 7 months; all acquitted on appeal in Aug 1986. Only 8 settlements covered deaths. The case went to the Truth Commission in 2014, which sought to take it to the Inter-American system.
summary: Gasoline from a Petrobras pipeline ignited under stilt houses. Nobody was held responsible in the end. The warning came from the Petrobras president, not an engineer.
